about: The golden set (scripts/eval/golden.mjs): fixed cases two configs are compared on, side by side. After Dark cases are production pairs (David's own characters and this season's house cast) run through POST /api/jobs/eval-after-dark, each with a scripted steer per step (direction[i] steers step i+1) so every run is comparable. Date cases are the date eval's fixed set (lib/eval.ts EVAL_CASES), run through POST /api/jobs/eval on two deployments. Optional `sheets` (by character id) override the sheet the judge reads; otherwise house and eval characters come from lib/eval.ts and the rest from the database (--db, read-only).

after_dark.why: two of David's characters: does each keep their own voice once it turns explicit, and does their date carry over?
direction: Pick up right after their date: one of them brings up something the other said there.
Chud explains how something works, confidently and wrongly, and Star teases him for it.
One of them suggests going somewhere more private, and the other has to say yes first.
Slow down for a moment: something honest about why each of them said yes tonight.

after_dark.why: calm and exact against loud and fast: two opposite voices that flatten into the same lines when the writer drifts
direction: Sable has three plans for the night at once; Cass picks one, precisely.
A sudden loud noise makes Cass flinch, and Sable notices.
Sable dares Cass to do something; Cass agrees, on her own terms.
They end up somewhere quieter, and it gets closer.

after_dark.why: the pair David has watched most: catchphrase repeats, moves nobody agreed to, memories that aren't there
direction: Sable says yes to a plan before Chud has finished explaining it.
Chud tries to follow the instructions for something and wings it instead.
One of them checks the time, and the other calls it out.
They agree to go back to one of their places.

after_dark.why: precision against improvisation: tells and sheet details (her right angles, his manuals) should show up in what they do
direction: Cass straightens things on the table while they talk, and Chud asks why.
Chud admits he never reads the instructions; Cass is horrified and charmed.
Cass suggests they leave, and Chud has to agree first.
Somewhere private, Cass explains flowers like explosives, and it turns into flirting.

dates.why: a thin visitor sheet against a rich house voice; misgendering; profile reading
two strong, opposite voices (showman vs deadpan)
a visitor with a full private soul
a show format with a named chaperone
a speed date (fewer turns) must still reach its ending
